issue_context.title: server: tenant remains writable even after service mode is stopped
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Related discussion in https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C03JCUUSCD6/p1735407188845879?thread_ts=1734543915.272749&cid=C03JCUUSCD6.

Shared tenants undergo a graceful draining process once we stop a tenant's service. When the tenant's service mode transitions to none, there may still be existing connections to the tenant, and these connections can still write to the tenant. 

**To Reproduce**
```
cockroach start-single-node --insecure

# Create a new tenant via the system tenant.
create tenant "test-tenant";
alter tenant "test-tenant" start service shared;

# Connect to the test tenant.
cockroach sql --url "postgresql://root@localhost:26257/cluster:test-tenant/defaultdb?sslmode=disable"
set cluster setting server.shutdown.drain_wait = '100s'; (or server.shutdown.connection_wait)

# Stop the tenant in the system tenant.
alter tenant "test-tenant" stop service;
show tenants -> wait until service mode is none

# Write/query from the test tenant.
create table foo (a int)
select * from foo
```

**Expected behavior**

We expect that there should be no draining process whenever a tenant transitions from external/shared to stopping, and finally to none. When the service mode is none, we should guarantee that the tenant is no longer accessible and writable.


Jira issue: CRDB-46023

review_comments: why does this require adding a new service mode which has more to do with the tenant deployment style (shared or external)? why not use a `TenantDataState`?

DataState describes the state of their persisted data, not their service. E.g. if you are half-way done restoring or importing or reverting them then their data is inconsistent, so it is not "ready", vs if their data is correct it is ready to server... but you still get to choose if and how to actually serve it. That actual choice is separate, and represented by svc mode.
Also note that this "new service mode" isn't all that new: we started adding it back in back in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/117677.
